record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Kirby Baker, Georges Mac Nulty and Walter Taylor have shown that the pattern abXbcY caZbaT ac is 4-avoidable, but not 3-avoidable [7]. What is the minimal proportion of the fourth letter needed to avoid that pattern?

evidence.quote: Kirby Baker, Georges Mac Nulty and Walter Taylor have shown that the pattern abXbcY caZbaT ac is 4-avoidable, but not 3-avoidable [7]. What is the minimal proportion of the fourth letter needed to avoid that pattern?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An infinite word $w$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$ is said to avoid a pattern $p$ (a word over a separate alphabet of variables) if there is no nonerasing morphism $h$ from the variable alphabet to $\Sigma^+$ such that $h(p)$ occurs as a factor of $w$. A pattern is called $k$-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over a $k$-letter alphabet that avoids it.

Consider the pattern
$$P = abXbcYcaZbaTac,$$
where $a,b,c$ are pattern variables and $X,Y,Z,T$ are pattern variables (each variable to be replaced by a nonempty word). It is known that $P$ is $4$-avoidable but not $3$-avoidable.

For an infinite word $w$ over a $4$-letter alphabet $\{1,2,3,4\}$ that avoids $P$, define the proportion of the letter $4$ in $w$ as
$$\rho_4(w) = \liminf_{n\to\infty} \frac{|w[1..n]|_4}{n},$$
where $|u|_4$ denotes the number of occurrences of the letter $4$ in $u$.

Determine
$$\inf\{\rho_4(w) : w \text{ is an infinite word over } \{1,2,3,4\} \text{ avoiding } P\}.$$
That is, find the minimal proportion of the fourth letter needed to avoid the pattern $abXbcYcaZbaTac$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return a definitive resolution of the minimal proportion of the fourth letter required to avoid the pattern $abXbcYcaZbaTac$. Related work on avoidable formulas and patterns in combinatorics on words (e.g., Clark's thesis on avoidable formulas, and Ochem's work on letter frequencies) discusses similar questions, but no explicit solved value for this specific pattern's minimal fourth-letter density was located.
